title: The Divinity of the Holy Spirit
author: Dn Yonnas
summary: A Scriptural study of the divinity of the Holy Spirit, showing that He possesses the very attributes of God: Creator, all-knowing, omnipresent, the giver of resurrection life, and the revealer of the future. It confesses the Holy Spirit as true God, of one essence with the Father and the Son, proceeding from the Father alone.

sections.h2: Introduction: The Lord, the Giver of Life

sections.p: The Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church confesses, with the Nicene-Constantinopolitan Creed, faith in the Holy Spirit, the Lord and Giver of life, who proceeds from the Father, who with the Father and the Son together is worshipped and glorified, who spoke by the prophets. The Holy Spirit is not a creature, nor an impersonal force, nor a created power; He is true God, the third Person of the Holy Trinity, of one essence with the Father and the Son.

Against those who would deny the Spirit's divinity (the Pneumatomachi, the “Spirit-fighters”), and against the Western addition of the Filioque, the Church teaches that the Holy Spirit proceeds from the Father alone, as the Lord Himself taught (John 15:26). The proof of His Godhead is that the attributes which belong to God alone are ascribed in Scripture to the Holy Spirit. This study sets out those attributes in order.

sections.h2: A. God Is the Creator; the Holy Spirit Is the Creator

sections.p: Genesis 1:1-2 reads: “In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth. And the earth was without form, and void; and darkness was upon the face of the deep. And the Spirit of God moved upon the face of the waters.” At the very dawn of creation the Spirit of God is present and active, brooding over the waters and bringing order out of the formless deep. The work of creation is the work of the one God, accomplished by the Father through the Son in the Holy Spirit. Since to create is the act of God alone, the Spirit's part in creation reveals Him to be God.

sections.h2: B. God Knows Everything; the Holy Spirit Knows Everything

sections.p: 1 Corinthians 2:9-10 declares that the things which God has prepared, which eye has not seen nor ear heard, “God hath revealed them unto us by his Spirit: for the Spirit searcheth all things, yea, the deep things of God.” The Spirit searches even the depths of God Himself. No creature can know the deep things of God; as the next verse says, only the Spirit of God knows the things of God, just as a man's own spirit knows the things of the man. The Holy Spirit therefore possesses the omniscience proper to God.

Acts 13:2-3 shows the same divine knowledge in action: “the Holy Ghost said, Separate me Barnabas and Saul for the work whereunto I have called them.” The Spirit speaks, calls servants to His work, and directs the Church. He speaks as God who knows His own purposes and commissions His own ministers.

sections.h2: C. God Is Omnipresent; the Holy Spirit Is Omnipresent

sections.p: Psalm 139:7-9 asks: “Whither shall I go from thy spirit? or whither shall I flee from thy presence? If I ascend up into heaven, thou art there: if I make my bed in hell, behold, thou art there. If I take the wings of the morning, and dwell in the uttermost parts of the sea; even there shall thy hand lead me.” The Psalmist identifies the Spirit's presence with God's own presence, and confesses that there is no place in all creation where the Spirit is not. To be present everywhere, filling heaven and earth, is an attribute of God alone. The Holy Spirit is omnipresent and therefore God.

sections.h2: D. God Raises the Dead; the Holy Spirit Raises the Dead

sections.p: Romans 8:11 teaches: “But if the Spirit of him that raised up Jesus from the dead dwell in you, he that raised up Christ from the dead shall also quicken your mortal bodies by his Spirit that dwelleth in you.” The resurrection of the dead, the restoration of life to mortal bodies, is the work of God; and Scripture attributes this quickening power to the indwelling Spirit. The Spirit is the Lord and Giver of life, both of the new life of grace now and of the resurrection of the body to come.

sections.h2: E. God Alone Knows the Future; the Holy Spirit Revealed the Future to the Prophets

sections.p: 2 Peter 1:21 states that prophecy “came not in old time by the will of man: but holy men of God spake as they were moved by the Holy Ghost.” The prophets did not foresee the future by their own power; they spoke as the Holy Spirit moved them. Since God alone truly knows things to come, the Spirit who reveals the future to the prophets is God. This is why the Creed says of Him, “who spoke by the prophets.”

Luke 12:11-12 records the Lord's promise that when His disciples are brought before rulers, “the Holy Ghost shall teach you in the same hour what ye ought to say.” The Spirit teaches and gives words in the moment of need, knowing what must be said. Acts 6:10 shows this fulfilled in Stephen, whose adversaries “were not able to resist the wisdom and the spirit by which he spake.” The wisdom of the Holy Spirit is divine and irresistible.

sections.h2: F. The Sayings of the Lord Jesus Christ Concerning the Spirit

sections.p: The clearest witness is the teaching of the Lord Himself, who in John 4:24 declares, “God is a Spirit: and they that worship him must worship him in spirit and in truth.” God is by nature Spirit; and the Holy Spirit, sharing the one divine nature, is rightly worshipped and glorified together with the Father and the Son.

Luke 3:21-22 records the Baptism of the Lord, when the heavens were opened, the Holy Spirit descended in bodily shape like a dove upon Him, and the Father's voice was heard from heaven. Here the three Persons of the Holy Trinity are revealed together: the Father speaking, the Son baptized, and the Holy Spirit descending. The Spirit appears as a distinct Person alongside the Father and the Son, not as a power emanating from them but as one of the three who share the one Godhead. This theophany at the Jordan is the great revelation of the Trinity.

John 14:16 records the Lord's promise: “And I will pray the Father, and he shall give you another Comforter, that he may abide with you for ever.” The Spirit is called “another Comforter,” of the same kind as the Son, a Person who abides with the Church forever. Concerning His origin the Lord teaches in John 15:26 that the Comforter “proceedeth from the Father,” and so the Church confesses the procession of the Holy Spirit from the Father alone, rejecting the addition of the Filioque.

sections.h2: Conclusion: Glory Be to the Holy Trinity

sections.p: The witness of Scripture is consistent and clear. The Holy Spirit is Creator, all-knowing, omnipresent, the giver of resurrection life, and the revealer of things to come; these are the attributes of God alone. He is revealed as a distinct Person at the Jordan, worshipped and glorified with the Father and the Son. Therefore the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church confesses the Holy Spirit as true God, of one essence with the Father and the Son, proceeding from the Father alone.

The Holy Trinity is one essence in three Persons: the Father unbegotten, the Son eternally begotten of the Father, and the Holy Spirit eternally proceeding from the Father, undivided in nature, glory, and worship.

sections.quote: Glory be to the Holy Trinity, the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit, ONE GOD. Amen.
